evidence.quote: In the present study, we extend such a chemical approach to the low-mass Class I source IRAS 04365+2535 in TMC-1A, whose luminosity is 2.5 $L_\odot$ (Green et al. 2013).

findings_qualitative.value: CS shows infalling-rotating motion; rotation disappears at ~50 AU; infalling gas distribution asymmetric

evidence.quote: The rotation motion traced by CS abruptly disappears around the radius of 50 AU from the protostar

findings_qualitative.value: SO is concentrated around the centrifugal barrier, more compact than CS

evidence.quote: the distribution is concentrated around the protostar, and is more compact than that of CS.

claims.hypothesis: CS kinematics in TMC-1A trace an infalling-rotating envelope rather than a Keplerian disk
claims.experiment: PV diagrams compared with a ballistic model
claims.result: rCB=50 AU, M=0.25 Msun, i=20 deg reproduce the PV diagrams
claims.finding: Infalling-rotating envelope conserving angular momentum down to ~50 AU

evidence.quote: It is well explained by a ballistic model of an infalling-rotating envelope with the radius of the centrifugal barrier (a half of the centrifugal radius) of 50 AU

claims.hypothesis: A chemical change occurs at the centrifugal barrier as in L1527
claims.experiment: Compare CS and SO distributions with model barrier
claims.result: SO concentrated near the barrier, CS outside
claims.finding: Infalling material is chemically processed (probably by accretion shock) before entering the disk

evidence.quote: a drastic change in chemical composition of the gas infalling onto the protostar is found to occur at a 50 AU scale probably due to accretion shocks

why_this_method.value: Simple ballistic model used because the main purpose is to account for velocity structure

evidence.quote: Since our main purpose is to account for the velocity structure, we simply assume an $r^{-1.5}$ density profile

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Keplerian disk cannot explain CS features

evidence.quote: All these characteristic features seen in the CS emission cannot be explained by a Keplerian disk
our ballistic model could be oversimplified
